text:
mika: quick sanity check — brought up argo-slim-embed v0.9 (int8 per-channel) on the short-query benchmark this morning and seeing a small recall hit vs baseline. recall@1 went from 0.713 -> 0.682, recall@5 0.892 -> 0.874, recall@10 0.936 -> 0.927. anyone free to help triage? :eyes:

sunil: can you paste the eval command & config? batch size, dim, index params etc?

mika: yep. run command and snippet:```bash
./eval_embeddings --model argo-slim-v0.9-int8 --dataset short-queries --k 1,5,10 --dim 768 --batch 64 --index hnsw --ef_search 128 --ef_construction 200
```
results csv header: `q_id,baseline_sim,new_sim,baseline_rank,new_rank` — attaching small sample inline:```
q1,0.84,0.81,1,2
q7,0.79,0.70,1,3
q12,0.65,0.66,2,2
```

tara: a couple quick things — 1) did we run with the same normalization? int8 path sometimes drops the float L2 norm step if the pipeline differs. 2) are KV cache/prefix caching behavioral differences possible for these short queries?

mika: normalizing with L2 post-quant, same preprocessing script used. caching shouldn't affect offline recall but i can re-run with explicit l2-normalize step to be sure.

jordan: could be index sensitivity. small recall deltas often due to ef_search or pq params. try ef_search=256 and see if recall@1 closes. also check exact nearest neighbor (brute) for a few failing queries to see if embedding similarity actually changed vs index artifact.

mika: good call. i'll run brute force on the top 50 fail cases and ef_search sweep. planning runs now, will paste logs.

ci-bot: batch-job 87321 finished — eval/argo-slim-v0.9-int8 on short-queries (64b) — 50 queries sampled, wall 00:06:12, mem 18GB

sunil: if brute shows the hit persists then we should compare per-dim delta heatmap and top-k token influence (e.g., which tokens' gradients changed under quantization). also try symmetric vs asymmetric quant for per-channel.

tara: also run a small UMAP on baseline vs int8 embeddings (colored by cluster id) — if clusters are shifting or merging that's a red flag for semantic collapse in rare classes.

mika: running brute and UMAP now. quick interim: ef_search=256 bumped recall@1 from 0.682 -> 0.695, but still below baseline. will post brute results in ~15m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

jordan: sweet. if brute agrees we should capture a few example pairs (orig top1 vs new top1) and add to the eval dashboard for quality review. might be acceptable for some customers but flag in rollout. :white_check_mark:
